== Enshrined God ==
The following two deities are enshrined.<ref>The notation and pronunciation of the enshrined deities are based on the shrine history book and the explanation board within the precincts. </ref>.
; Main enshrined deity
:* '''Nakatsushima Hime no Mikoto'' (Nakatsushima Hime no Mikoto) - Another name is {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|Ichikishima-hime|zh|市寸島比賣命|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishima Hime no Mikoto}} (Ichikishima Hime no Mikoto).
; Deity enshrined
:* Ikudama no Kami - The history of his enshrinement is unknown {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1987}}.

As a different theory, ``{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記|qid=Q11604964}}'' states that ``Kisansho Shrine'' enshrines the three deities of Idakeso (Itake no Mikoto, Oyatsuhime no Mikoto, and Tomatsuhime no Mikoto), and assumes that the deity enshrined at Shima Shrine is Oyatsuhime no Mikoto {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. However, since Shima Shrine is located on Kawanakajima in {{ill|Kinokawa River|arz|نهر كينوكاوا|fr|Kino-kawa|ja|紀の川|ko|기노카와강|my|ခိနိုခဝမြစ်|ro|Kinokawa (râu)|ru|Кинокава (река)|uk|Кінокава|zh|紀之川|qid=Q1042624}}, Nakatsushima Hime no Mikoto is appropriate from the location point of view {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}.

Also, in "{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|ja|住吉大社神代記|qid=Q11381815}}," Funatama Shrine in the {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|de|Sumiyoshi-Taisha|es|Sumiyoshi Taisha|fa|سومییوشی-تایشا|fi|Sumiyoshi-taisha|fr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|it|Grande santuario di Sumiyoshi|ja|住吉大社|ko|스미요시 대사|la|Sumiyoshi-taisha|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနန်းကွန်းနန်းရင်း|pt|Sumiyoshi taisha|ru|Сумиёси-тайся|sl|Veliko svetišče Sumijoši-taiša|th|ศาลเจ้าซูมิโยชิ|tr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|uk|Сумійосі тайся|zh|住吉大社|qid=Q705949}} Setsusha is said to be the deity of the Ki clan and the headquarters of ``Shima-kami, Shizuka-kami, and Date-kami'' {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}.

Currently, as the place name ``{{ill|Nakanoshima|ja|中之島 (和歌山市)|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}'' indicates, it is located on an island in the {{ill|Kinokawa River|arz|نهر كينوكاوا|fr|Kino-kawa|ja|紀の川|ko|기노카와강|my|ခိနိုခဝမြစ်|ro|Kinokawa (râu)|ru|Кинокава (река)|uk|Кінокава|zh|紀之川|qid=Q1042624}} delta, but the company name ``Shima'' is said to refer to Kawanakajima.{{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. Before Hiden, our company was called ``Kuzu Myojin (Kunizu Myojin),'' and at the time of the Genna era, there were six small shrines on the island, including our company, but Kuzu Myojin was chosen because it had the best location.{{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}

== Festival ==
The main festivals are as follows. <ref> Festival descriptions are from [http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=1032 Shima Shrine] (Wakayama Prefectural Shrine Agency). </ref>.
* Star Festival Setsubun Festival (February 3rd)
* Summer Festival (Yoimiya July 14th, Hongu Shrine July 15th)
*Children's mikoshi togyo (2nd Saturday of July)
* Annual festival (October 15th)
* Niwakuri ritual (night of December 15th)

== Cultural assets ==

== Cultural property designated by Wakayama Prefecture ==
*Tangible cultural property
** Shima Shrine Main Hall (with 26 ridge tags, 1 pair of lion and guardian dog) (building) - Designated on March 18, 2022 <ref>{{PDFlink|[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/010100/kenpou/d00209691_d/fil/r0403180295.pdf From Wakayama Prefectural Newsletter, March 18, 2020] Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education Notice No. 1 (link to Wakayama Prefecture homepage). </ref>.
